items.title: Headlines for November 17, 2026 | Democracy Now!
items.excerpt: ## Trump Arrives in Philippines Ahead of ASEAN Summit and Meeting with Putin, Xi Nov 17, 2026 President Trump has arrived in the Philippines on the first leg of a 48-hour trip to Asia. Trump landed in Manila aboard the new Air Force One, a luxury 747 jet gifted to him by the government of Qatar. He’s scheduled to meet with President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. ahead of the ASEAN summit of Southeast Asian nations. Trump’s visit has drawn large protests in Manila, where police arrested hundreds of people over the weekend. Students, workers and progressive groups are demanding an end to the U.S. and Israeli war on Iran and are protesting against plans to build an artificial intelligence and manufacturing hub near Manila. On Thursday, Trump will hold an unprecedented trilateral summit in Shenzhen, China, with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin. Trump also said he might meet with North Korean leader Kim Jong-un while in China. ## Trump Says He “Would Not Mind” Seeing Jensen Huang Restored as CEO of Nvidia Nov 17, 2026 The Trump administration said Monday it would investigate Megaspeed, the Singapore-based cloud computing firm that’s accused of sending advanced Nvidia computer chips to China, in violation of U.S. export controls. The investigation follows Nvidia founder Jensen Huang’s resignation as CEO, after he admitted he’d had an extramarital affair with former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang. Megaspeed said on Sunday she had left the company more than a year ago. On Monday, President Trump responded to reports that Jensen Huang is in discussions with allies about a potential return to Nvidia. > Reporter: “Mr. President, do you want to see Jensen Huang reinstated as CEO of Nvidia?” > President Donald Trump: “I would — I would not mind. I would not mind that. I like — you know, I threw out the name of Tim Cook. But I would say that the — Jensen’s reinstatement, I think he learned a big lesson, I guess maybe one lesson more important than another. But I would certainly not mind seeing that.” ## Trump Takes “No Responsibility” for Largest FAA Ground Stop Since 9/11 Nov 17, 2026 United Airlines canceled dozens of departing flights and delayed more than 800 others on Monday after a system outage that lasted more than 90 minutes. United blamed a “technical issue,” without elaborating, and said in a statement there was “no indication that this was a cybersecurity-related issue.” This comes after the FAA ordered a nearly five-hour nationwide ground stop on Friday, causing over 18,000 flight cancellations and more than 28,000 delays. It was the largest disruption of its kind to U.S. air travel since the 9/11 attacks. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy is due to brief senators about the incident today. On Monday, President Trump said Duffy had his full support, and blamed the Biden administration for the grounded flights. > President Donald Trump: “I don’t take any responsibility. They did a great job. Secretary Duffy, they acted incredibly. Everybody was safe. Nobody was hurt. No crashes, no nothing.” Shortly after taking office in January 2025, Trump signed an executive order freezing the remaining funds in a $25 billion Biden-era appropriation to modernize flight infrastructure. ... ## Israel Failed to Meet Commitments to Deliver Food and Supplies to Gaza Nov 17, 2026 In Gaza, Israeli forces killed a young Palestinian man and wounded others in an attack east of the city of Deir al-Balah in central Gaza. Elsewhere, Israeli forces killed one Palestinian and injured five in the north, while in southern Gaza, Israeli forces shot and wounded three Palestinians, including a child, inside a school. The latest killings come as Israel has failed to meet its aid commitments under the Gaza ceasefire deal. Data obtained by Haaretz showed decreasing food deliveries to Gaza, alongside severe shortages of medical supplies, tents and materials to repair damaged infrastructure. The U.N. is also urging the protection of aid workers and hospitals. This is U.N. spokesperson Farhan Haq. > Farhan Haq: “Yesterday, an Israeli airstrike hit very close to a U.N.-led fuel convoy in Rafah. We are concerned that strikes at targets near our staff and vehicles, especially vehicles carrying fuel, expose them to unacceptable risks. Civilians, including humanitarian workers, must always be protected.” ## Israeli Opposition Slams Netanyahu’s “Attempted Coup” over Framed Arab MKs ... The report also said ... ## Iran Attacks U.S. Radar Station in Bahrain, Says It Captured U.S. Drone Nov 17, 2026 Bahrain’s military says it intercepted an Iranian drone strike targeting a U.S. radar facility — the third attack of its kind in recent days. The assault came after U.S. Central Command announced a third carrier strike group, the USS Theodore Roosevelt, had arrived in the Middle East, adding about 10,000 sailors and Marines to U.S. forces in the region. Meanwhile, Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps says it had hacked the flight guidance system of a U.S.-made MQM-170 drone and landed it remotely, intact. It’s the latest in a series of similar claims by Iran. Meanwhile, three more vessels caught fire while transiting the Strait of Hormuz today, including a ship carrying liquefied natural gas and a supertanker holding more than 2 million barrels of crude oil. ## Ukrainian Strike Damages Bridge Linking Crimea to Russia Russia reports that Ukraine has carried out its largest drone strike of the war so far. According to Moscow, the attack damaged the major bridge connecting Russia with occupied Crimea and struck several oil refineries. Russian officials say their forces shot down over 2,000 drones and four long-range Flamingo missiles in a 24-hour period. Moscow’s mayor said about 600 of those drones were aimed at the capital. Meanwhile, Kyiv had 17 air raid alerts in one day, the most on record. Russian strikes killed at least seven people in Ukraine, as attacks on energy infrastructure left 50,000 people without power.

items.title: National and International News in Focus: Nov. 17 | National | wktv.com
items.excerpt: ## Trump arrives in Philippines to kick off Asia trip with economic deals and talks with allies ... ## Ousted Nvidia CEO Huang agrees to questioning by US lawmakers WASHINGTON (AP) — Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has agreed to appear for transcribed interviews as the company faces national security scrutiny over its chip sales. Huang will speak to House and Congress lawmakers on December 1, followed by Nvidia's general counsel Tim Teter on December 2. Lawmakers want answers about Nvidia's role in allowing Chinese actors access to advanced chips. Nvidia announced a new board committee to oversee national security and trade compliance. This follows revelations of Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Nvidia's advanced chips are crucial for AI but face sales restrictions to China. ## A 2-month lull ends with Iran’s third strike on US targets in Bahrain CAIRO (AP) — Iran has fired drones at a U.S. radar facility in Bahrain. The move on Tuesday was Iran's third attack on American military targets in the kingdom in recent days as Tehran resumed strikes on its Arab neighbors after a two-month lull. Bahrain said that its air defenses intercepted the drones. The attacks come as the USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier strike group arrived in the region to expand U.S. military firepower amid the nearly nine-month war. Iran says the strikes were in retaliation for U.S. attacks and drone surveillance operations. Analysts say Tehran’s growing economic pressures and stalled peace negotiations are raising the risk of renewed escalation as Washington weighs its next move. ## Ukrainian drones and missiles strike Kerch Bridge that links Russia with Crimea KYIV, Ukraine (AP) — Ukrainian drones and missiles struck the vital Kerch Bridge linking Russia to the occupied Crimean Peninsula. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy announced the strike Tuesday, calling the operation “unprecedented." Russia reported that its forces downed a record number of Ukrainian drones for the second straight day. Zelenskyy portrayed the bridge operation as a masterstroke following a weekslong effort by Ukrainian forces to gradually wear down Russian air defenses before bombarding the prized target. Russia’s top criminal investigation agency acknowledged that the bridge was attacked and damaged but didn’t elaborate.

items.title: US import prices rise more than expected in October By Reuters
items.excerpt: WASHINGTON, Nov 17 (Reuters) - US import prices increased more than expected in October, the latest indication that inflation pressures were broadening beyond energy goods. Import prices advanced 1.1% last month after rising by the same margin in September, the Labor Department’s Bureau of Labor Statistics said on Tuesday. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast import prices, which exclude tariffs, climbing 0.7%. The BLS did not publish year-over-year import price readings because last year’s federal government shutdown prevented the collection of data in October 2025, leaving no comparison base. Imported inflation accelerated 8.1% in September, the largest gain in just more than four years. The government last week reported stronger-than-expected consumer prices in October as well as firmer producer inflation details, reinforcing economists’ views inflation was broadening beyond the energy sector as the US-Israeli war with Iran drags on. Economists expect the Federal Reserve to continue raising interest rates after next month’s widely expected hike. Financial markets have priced in a 25-basis-point rate hike in December and anticipated another increase in borrowing costs in January, CME’s FedWatch tool showed. The Fed left its benchmark overnight interest rate in the 3.75%-4.00% range last month. Import prices were last month driven by a 3.6% rise in the cost of fuels. That followed a 6.3% jump in September. There were also increases in the prices of petroleum and natural gas. Imported food prices fell 0.2% after rising 0.4% in September. Excluding the fuels and food, import prices shot up 0.9% after increasing 0.5% in September. Prices of imported capital goods soared 1.5%, driven by a 1.7% jump in the cost of nonelectrical machinery. That is likely related to the AI infrastructure buildout. Imported capital goods prices advanced 1.0% in September. Imported automotive vehicles, parts and engines prices increased 0.4% after gaining 0.3% in September. Prices for consumer goods, excluding automotives, rose 0.5% after climbing 0.3% in September.

items.title: Fed’s Musalem: US likely needs several rate hikes by spring to control inflation By Reuters
items.excerpt: WASHINGTON, Nov 17 (Reuters) - The US Federal Reserve many need several rate hikes to bring high inflation under control and should act soon to ensure the problem doesn’t get worse, St. Louis Fed president Alberto Musalem said on Tuesday. "The economy will likely require several interest rate increases before the spring of 2027 to achieve price stability in a timely manner," Musalem said, arguing that the current policy rate, in the 3.75% to 4% range, is as much as a percentage point below where it needs to be to return inflation to the Fed’s 2% target. It is currently running above 3%, and Musalem said the most likely scenario is that it remains elevated unless the Fed acts. The Fed next meets on Dec. 8-9 and is expected to approve a quarter percentage point rate hike. Musalem is not a voter on interest rate policy this year. "Inflation is too high...Looking ahead, risks are skewed toward persistent above-target inflation," with current policy not acting as significant restraint on growth that continues above trend, Musalem said in remarks prepared for delivery to a Central Bank of Argentina conference in Buenos Aires. "Moving sooner, while inflation expectations are anchored, has a better chance of succeeding without adverse impact on the labor market or economic growth," he said.

items.title: Fed’s Williams says more rate hikes likely needed amid inflation By Investing.com
items.excerpt: Investing.com -- Federal Reserve Bank of New York President John Williams said Tuesday the US central bank will likely need to raise interest rates again to address high inflation but dismissed calls for more aggressive policy action. Speaking at the Axios BFD Annual Summit in New York, Williams acknowledged inflation remains elevated. "Inflation is 'stubbornly high,'" he said, adding that the Fed is "seeing signs of shocks spilling over into broader inflation data." Williams noted that tariffs and energy shocks continue to affect inflation readings. He said the economy is strong and getting stronger, while inflation is not moving in the right direction. The New York Fed president said the current approach does not require a major shift in strategy. "I don't think the situation calls for dramatic policy action," Williams stated. He added, "I think what we've been doing over the last, past few months … is working well." Williams emphasized the Fed's commitment to its inflation target. "We still have our work to do to make sure that we bring inflation back down to 2% in a timely way and in a sustained manner," he said. He later stated the Fed "will get inflation back to 2% in a timely manner."

items.title: Citi sees early signs of energy pass through By Investing.com
items.excerpt: Published Nov 17, 2026, 11:35 AM ... Investing.com -- Citi told clients in a note Tuesday that October’s consumer price data may offer the clearest signs yet that higher energy and transport costs are filtering through to other prices, though it cautioned that more data is needed to confirm the trend. Core CPI rose 0.3% in October, the third straight month of stronger-than-expected readings. Citi now expects core PCE inflation, the Fed’s preferred gauge, to rise to 3.2% year over year in October. “Some details of October data may offer the clearest signs yet that higher input and transportation costs are pushing up other prices,” the bank wrote. October showed unusually large increases in household furnishings, restaurants, medical goods, car insurance and local transport such as taxis. Citi said higher taxi fares very likely reflect gas prices, while stronger furnishings prices may reflect higher shipping costs. “But we also remain cautious that data has been much more volatile than usual, and more months of data will be needed to judge the degree of pass through,” Citi said. The bank noted that core CPI was flat as recently as June. It also warned that annual inflation readings for October and November will be distorted upward by last year’s government shutdown, before normalizing with December data. Citi expects the next four months of inflation data to be strong, though it sees downside risks to high expectations in the first quarter. Factors that boosted early 2026 inflation, such as airfares, may be weaker this time. “If rising prices do reflect more energy price pass-through, we would expect some stickiness to stronger increases, with prices continuing to rise over the next few months,” the bank added.

items.title: Economy, the Fed, and Rates…
items.excerpt: November 17, 2026 Economic Data & Labor Market - Consumer inflation strengthened the case for further Fed increases. The Consumer Price Index rose 0.4% in October after September's 0.6% increase, and the core index, which excludes food and energy, rose 0.3%, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported on November 10. Both exceeded Bloomberg's survey medians by 0.1 percentage point; shelter increased 0.3% and energy 0.7%. BLS did not publish 12-month CPI changes because it did not collect October 2025 data during the government shutdown, making the monthly readings particularly important for assessing current inflation. - Producer inflation extended beyond energy. Prices received by producers for final-demand goods and services rose 0.3% in October and 6.5% over 12 months, the fastest annual increase since November 2022, BLS reported on November 13. Excluding food, energy, and trade services, prices rose 0.5% on the month and 4.9% over the year. The slower headline monthly gain, following September's revised 1.4% increase, therefore did not signal a broad retreat in price pressure. - Home sales fell to their slowest pace since 2010. Existing-home sales fell 5.5% in October to a 3.75 million annual rate, the lowest since August 2010, the National Association of Realtors reported on November 12. Sales were 8.8% below a year earlier, and inventory reached 1.59 million homes, or 5.1 months of supply. The median price was $416,700, up 0.4% from a year earlier, indicating that weak turnover has not yet brought substantial nationwide price relief. ... - Layoffs remained low, but inflation absorbed wage gains. Initial unemployment claims increased 9,000 to 200,000 for the week ended November 7, from an upwardly revised 191,000; the four-week average was unchanged at 195,250. Continuing claims fell 20,000 to 1.697 million for the week ended October 31. Separately, BLS reported that inflation-adjusted average hourly and weekly earnings were unchanged in October, as a 0.4% rise in nominal hourly pay was offset by consumer inflation, leaving workers without an improvement in purchasing power. ... - Officials opened the door to larger or faster rate increases. Governor Christopher Waller said on November 10 that he supported at least a quarter-point December increase and would consider a half-point if October core CPI rose 0.3% or more, a threshold the subsequent release met. Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan called for at least two more quarter-point increases. New York Fed President John Williams said on November 12 that additional increases would likely be needed, reinforcing the prospect of further tightening beyond December.

items.excerpt: ## Alaska midterm race could be called on Wednesday as Peltola remains ahead of Republican incumbent Hello and welcome to the US politics live blog. The final Senate race of this year’s midterm elections could be resolved tomorrow if Alaska election officials run the state’s ranked choice voting system to determine the result. With 98% of ballots counted, Democratic challenger Mary Peltola is out in front with 49.98% of the vote. By contrast, incumbent Republican senator Dan S Sullivan has a 45.93% share, according to the latest Associated Press figures. In terms of actual voting numbers, Peltola is ahead by just over 11,000, with 141,637 compared to Sullivan’s 130,162. All eyes will be on Peltola to see if she can keep the pace to achieve 50% of the ballot, two weeks on from the election. If not, then voters’ second choice votes will be counted. items.title: Democrats are still cautiously optimistic about an immigration deal with Trump - POLITICO
items.excerpt: 11/17/2026 4:45 AM EST In the days before the midterm election, Rep. Henry Cuellar (D-Texas) felt confident that a blue wave could open the door to immigration reform. Now Cuellar is one of several moderate Democrats angling to strike a deal with the White House, especially on reining in ICE officers and creating legal pathways to citizenship for some immigrants. Virginia Foxx of North Carolina said Monday that she has requested a recount in her reelection race, where she trails Democrat Chuck Hubbard by 331 votes. Unofficial totals show Hubbard with 139,770 votes and Foxx with 139,439, a margin within the 1 percent that state law allows for a recount. Foxx, an 11-term Republican, is the only Republican congressional candidate in the state to seek one. She said in a statement that she expects a smooth process that respects state law. The state elections board plans to finish a machine recount by Nov. 23 and to consider certification on Nov. 24.

She is up for album, record, and song of the year in the same year for the fifth time. Beyoncé became the first artist in history to land 100 lifetime Grammy nominations when her B’Day 20th anniversary reissue bonus track, “Morning Dew (Donk),” picked up a nod for best R&B solo performance. The song was released on July 4 and was written by Beyoncé, Pharrell Williams, The-Dream, and Darius Dixon and produced by Beyoncé and Pharrell. items.excerpt: ## 1. Six Nigerians on the 2027 Grammy list ### What happened The Recording Academy announced nominations for the 69th Grammy Awards on Monday. Nigerian acts hold four of the five spots in Best African Music Performance: Asake twice, for Gratitude and for Jogodo with Wizkid, Tems for Big Daddy, and Ayra Starr with Beninese singer Angélique Kidjo for Aye Kan (Are You Coming Back?). The fifth nominee is Ghana’s King Ayisoba with Rocky Dawuni. Three Nigerian albums are up for Best Global Music Album: Tems’ Love Is a Kingdom, Davido’s Oriadé and Ayra Starr’s Starrgirl. Burna Boy is nominated in Best Global Music Performance for Dai Dai, his World Cup song with Shakira. Tems also picked up R&B recognition for What You Need. Outlets count her total differently, with some listing three nominations and others four, because she appears as a songwriter in Best R&B Song as well as a performer. ### Why it matters Nigerian artists are now competing with each other for the same trophy, which says a lot about how far the sound has travelled. The ceremony is on 7 February 2027 at the Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles and will air on ABC and stream on Disney+ and Hulu. For background, see our ranking of the best Afrobeats albums of 2026. Source: ThisDay; TVC News; Peoples Gazette. ## 2. AMAA 2026: Kenya and Côte d’Ivoire lead, Nigeria picks up key prizes ### What happened The 22nd Africa Movie Academy Awards held on Sunday night at the Marriott Hotel in Ikeja, Lagos. One Woman One Bra, a Kenya-Nigeria co-production directed by Vincho Nchogu, won Best Film, Best Film in an African Language and Best Debut Feature. The Colour of Exile from Côte d’Ivoire won the most awards, four, including Best Director and Best Actress for Naky Sy Savane. Nigeria’s main winners were Wale Ojo (Best Actor, Lights Out), Linda Ejiofor (Best Supporting Actress, The Herd) and To Adaego With Love, which took Best Nigerian Film and the screenplay award. The Herd also won for production design and make-up, The Creek for visual effects, and Evi for soundtrack. ### Why it matters Nollywood still dominated the nomination lists, but the top prizes went elsewhere this year, a reminder that the rest of the continent’s film industry is growing fast too. Source: Channels TV; TheCable Lifestyle; Afrocritik. ## 3. Box office: Five Figurines on top, Agbara Nla keeps climbing ### Five Figurines and Issakaba Returns Akay Mason’s thriller Five Figurines, starring Bimbo Akintola and Odunlade Adekola, opened at number one over the 13 to 15 November weekend. Its distributors put the takings at more than ₦64.8 million and called it the biggest November opening for a Nollywood film. Industry tracker Fusion Intelligence reports about ₦64.4 million from 9,789 admissions, around 30 per cent of the weekend’s total, with Sunday alone bringing in ₦33.1 million. Issakaba Returns opened second with ₦44 million, or ₦46.5 million including previews. ### Agbara Nla: The Return passes ₦513 million Distributor Nile Entertainment said on Monday that the remake of Mike Bamiloye’s 1993 Christian classic has now made more than ₦513.4 million since it opened on 1 October. That makes it the second-biggest Nollywood film of 2026 behind Call of My Life, and the ninth-biggest Nollywood title ever. ... ## 4. Olamide drops Time and Space ### What happened Olamide released Time and Space on Monday through YBNL Nation and EMPIRE. It has 10 songs and runs about 32 minutes. FOLA is the only guest, on Jaiye, and October’s single Burukutu sits at track four. Olamide said he painted the cover art himself. The album follows his self-titled 2025 record, Olamidé, which had a much longer guest list.
